does: Boils rinsed and soaked rice in a large pot of well-salted water, with whole spices if the dish asks for them, only until each grain is nearly tender with a firm core, then drains it at once. The grains finish later, in steam, in a layered dish.

intro.what: This layered-rice method boils soaked grains only partway before draining for a later steaming stage.
intro.why: It teaches you to plan texture across successive cooking steps rather than finish the rice during the first boil.

how: Rinse the rice in several changes of cold water until the water is nearly clear, then leave it to soak in cold water for a good while and drain it.
Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil with plenty of salt, and the whole spices if there are any. The water should taste of the sea.
Slide in the rice, bring the water back to the boil and stir once, gently, to stop the grains sticking.
Test a grain often. It is ready when it snaps cleanly and shows a white, firm core when pressed between the fingers.
Drain it at once into a colander and spread it out. Do not rinse it. It must not be left to sit and go on cooking.

cues.text: A grain bends but then snaps, and the core is firm and chalky white.
The grains have grown long and are still separate, with no mush in the water.

mistakes.mistake: Boiling the rice until it is soft, so that it turns to paste during the final steaming.
mistakes.fix: Drain it while the core is still firm. It has a long steam still to come.

mistakes.mistake: Skipping the rinse and the soak, so that the grains clump and break.
mistakes.fix: Rinse until the water is nearly clear, then soak before boiling.

mistakes.mistake: Salting the water too lightly, so that the finished dish tastes flat.
mistakes.fix: Salt the water boldly. Most of it goes down the drain.

quiz.question: Why drain this rice while its core is still firm?
choices: It will be served immediately without further cooking.
It will soften further during the later steaming.
Its centre should remain dry in the finished dish.
quiz.because: The first boil is deliberately incomplete because the layered dish still has a steaming stage.

quiz.question: What should happen when the grains reach the intended firm-core stage?
choices: Leave them sitting in the hot water.
Drain promptly and spread them out.
quiz.because: Prompt draining limits further softening before the planned final steam.

quiz.question: Which texture fits rice at the end of parboiling?
choices: A grain bends then snaps with a firm chalky core.
A grain crushes into a completely soft paste.
A grain is unchanged and dry throughout.
quiz.because: The outside has softened while a firm core leaves room for the later cooking step.

quiz.question: Rice turns pasty during the final steam. What should change next time?
choices: Boil it fully soft before layering.
Stop the first boil while the core remains firm.
Leave drained rice in the hot cooking water.
quiz.because: Fully softening rice before steaming gives it more cooking than the intended texture can tolerate.

comes_after.why: Rice for layering must lose its loose starch first or it clumps, so rinsing comes before boiling.

variant_of.differs: The rice is boiled in a great deal of water, as pasta is, and drained while a firm core remains. It is not cooked in a measured amount of water until all the water is gone. The last of the cooking is done later in steam.
The food is rice, boiled in a large pot of well-salted water only until nearly tender, to be finished later by steaming.
